title: Introduce init-wave annotations and optional rollback-fence for private Helm installs
author: Marisol Chen
release_notes: Adds opt-in init-wave annotations, a rollback-fence annotation to protect tenant migrations, stricter Helm linting in CI, and extended values schema for private installs. No breaking changes by default; features are opt-in via values.yaml.
description:
Context and motivation: Private deployments sometimes need fine-grained control over how init jobs and Helm hooks are sequenced across tenants and multi-AZ migrations. Current init hooks run in a single phase which makes long-running tenant migrations and staged DB migrations fragile: a subsequent Helm rollback can unintentionally interrupt an in-flight tenant migration. This PR introduces two orthogonal features to improve safety and flexibility for private installs: 1) init-wave annotations: a lightweight mechanism to assign init hooks to ordered waves (0..N) and have the chart render sequenced Job resources; 2) rollback-fence annotation: an opt-in guard that prevents chart-level rollback (Helm uninstall/rollback) from running if a tenant-level fence label is present and migrate-in-progress is detected.

What this PR changes (high level): - values.schema.json: updated to include new fields under .private.initWaves and .private.rollbackFence with validation and defaults. - templates/init-wave-job.yaml: new template that renders init jobs grouped by wave, uses annotation "redwood.io/init-wave" to choose ordering and adds readinessProbe-based gate for longer-running migrations. - templates/rollback-fence-hook.yaml: new pre-delete hook that checks for fence label and fails early with a clear message when rollbackFence.enabled = true. - templates/_helpers.tpl: helper functions for wave sorting and fence message. - .github/workflows/helm-lint.yaml: enable strict lint stage and run chart testing with the new schema. - charts/README.md: docs for the new opt-in flags and recommended patterns for multi-tenant migrations. - tests/preflight-waves.yaml: integration-style smoke test that exercises three-wave sequencing in CI.

Commits (summary): - 7f3a2d2: Add values.schema.json entries and defaults for initWaves and rollbackFence. - 84b1c6f: Implement init-wave job template and helpers for sorting. - a2d9b7a: Add rollback-fence pre-delete hook and exit messages. - c1e4f5b: CI: enable helm lint strict and add simple chart-testing. - e0f6b2c: Docs: expand README and add examples for tenant migrations and fences.

Files touched (representative): - values.schema.json (new fields, validation) - templates/init-wave-job.yaml (new) - templates/rollback-fence-hook.yaml (new) - templates/_helpers.tpl (updated) - charts/README.md (updated) - .github/workflows/helm-lint.yaml (updated) - tests/preflight-waves.yaml (new) - templates/NOTES.txt (updated) - Chart.yaml (patch bump)

Behavior and compatibility notes: - All features are opt-in. By default the chart behavior is unchanged: if private.initWaves is empty, existing init hook behavior is preserved. - rollbackFence.enabled defaults to false. When enabled, the pre-delete hook will run and will fail the delete if a fence label ("redwood.io/migration-in-progress=true") is detected on any namespace-scoped resource the hook inspects. This is intentionally conservative to prevent accidental disruption. - The init-wave implementation orders waves numerically and runs sequentially. Within a wave, jobs run concurrently (same as traditional hooks). - The pre-delete hook is a lightweight guard and advises operators to run a controlled migration rollback procedure; it does not attempt automatic resolution.

Review discussion (highlights, chronological): - Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice approach, I like the opt-in nature. Two asks: 1) can the fence check be toggled to only scan a tenant label set to avoid scanning too broadly? 2) add a short-circuit on the pre-delete hook so quick deletes for dev clusters aren't blocked." - Marisol Chen (author reply): "Addressed both: added rollbackFence.scanScope with values [namespace|tenant|cluster] (default namespace) and added an override rollbackFence.bypassForTags for dev buckets. Updated schema and README examples." - Priya Nair (review): "Can we add a Prometheus metric or event when a fence prevents a delete so SRE can alert?" - Marisol Chen: "Added a note in the docs recommending customers emit an Event in the hook; kept metric emission out of the chart to avoid coupling to any metrics stack. Also added example snippet showing how to emit a k8s Event from the hook job." - Samir Gupta (requested change): "Make the wave sorting deterministic when custom labels are used (pad numbers)." - Marisol Chen: "Updated helper to zero-pad and to treat absent values as wave 0. Added unit test in templates using helm-unittest pattern." - Priya Nair (approve): "Approved after the schema tests pass." - Diego Alvarez (approve): "LGTM. Verified the smoke test in CI."

CI and checks: - helm-lint (strict): pass - chart-tests (preflight-waves): pass - unit-template-tests: pass - integration smoke job (k8s kind): pass (flake-free on rerun) Summary: CI green after two iterations; minor lint tweaks fixed in second commit.

Merge details: Squash-and-merge chosen. Merge commit authored by Marisol Chen with message "Introduce init-wave annotations and optional rollback-fence for private installs — opt-in safety for tenant migrations". Deployed a dry-run of the chart to our internal staging environment and ran the preflight-waves test to validate sequencing.

Operational guidance (brief): - To enable init waves: set private.initWaves:
    enabled: true
    waves:
      - name: db-migrate
        annotations:
          - key: redwood.io/init-wave
            value: "1"
  See charts/README.md for full examples. - To enable rollback guard: set private.rollbackFence.enabled = true and choose scanScope per your tenancy model. - For on-prem customers with long-running migrations, combine waves with readinessProbe gating to reduce accidental concurrency.

Related work and follow-ups: - ENG-4591 will add an optional controller-based fence for clusters that prefer an operator rather than a hook-based guard. - A follow-up PR will add an optional Prometheus metric emission when fences trigger (team agreed to keep that separate from the chart change to avoid dependency churn).
